title: Expanded brainstem and diencephalic source regions
author: NeuroImage project
objective: Study original healthy-source regional probabilities and independent masks in their supplied MRI context, with explicit limits for complexes, small samples and numbered subdivisions.

scenes.title: Vestibular and superior olivary source complexes
scenes.prompt: Compare the paired source complexes in complete FA sections, then magnify at the selected source point. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: The vestibular and superior olivary complexes are aggregate source regions. Component nuclei and nerve VIII courses require finer source definitions. These views support comparison of the delivered regional extents.

scenes.title: Medullary viscero-sensory-motor and inferior olivary context
scenes.prompt: Follow both source complexes through adjacent sections and compare their relation to the inferior olivary masks. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: VSM is one combined source region. Its aggregate definition provides the teaching context here; individual constituent nuclei and nerve IX-XII trajectories require separate source evidence.

scenes.title: Lateral and medial parabrachial source regions
scenes.prompt: Keep one field selected while comparing the four original mask surfaces and adjacent FA sections. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: The source masks retain population overlap at the original 0.35 threshold. Their surfaces describe thresholded population support; histological boundaries are a separate level of evidence.

scenes.title: Locus coeruleus and subcoeruleus source regions
scenes.prompt: Establish location in complete source sections before magnifying the small selected region. Switch selected fields to compare original support. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: Small source regions retain their original 1 mm sampling. This sampling governs contour detail. The atlas derives from the earlier healthy-volunteer acquisition cited alongside its later clinical application.

scenes.title: Source tegmental and pontine reticular complexes
scenes.prompt: Compare the delivered combined regions and inspect their original names in the source-definition panel. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: Compound source names and their combined regional definitions are retained. Interpret each complete source region using its original constituent description.

scenes.title: Cuneiform and pedunculotegmental source pairs
scenes.prompt: Inspect both source pairs in the supplied FA template and compare their location across all three section planes. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: The source list names PTg pedunculotegmental and also uses pedunculopontine. This view supports observation of the recorded regional position; function and connectivity have separate evidential requirements.

scenes.title: Left mesencephalic reticular source subdivisions
scenes.prompt: Compare the parent source field with its separately delivered anterior, dorsal and lateral fields. Hide surrounding surfaces to inspect one at a time. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: Parent and component probability fields are independent, potentially overlapping memberships. Each field keeps its original source definition and spatial samples.

scenes.title: Right mesencephalic reticular source subdivisions
scenes.prompt: Inspect the independently supplied right-sided fields and compare their definitions with the preceding left-sided view. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: The view uses the original right-sided fields. Population averaging and source sampling govern comparison of the two sides.

scenes.title: Left medullary reticular parents and components
scenes.prompt: Follow the source parent fields and their medial and lateral components. Read probability values before interpreting a small contour. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: The smallest component masks contain few original 1 mm samples. Surfaces retain that sampling, with simultaneous parent and component memberships.

scenes.title: Right medullary reticular parents and components
scenes.prompt: Inspect the source-defined right-sided components and compare nearby sections before isolating one surface. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: The two sides use independently supplied original fields. Their mask volumes describe this source release; population prevalence of anatomical asymmetry requires separate evidence.

scenes.title: Red nucleus and numbered source subregions
scenes.prompt: Compare the whole left red nucleus field with source subregions 1 and 2 by selecting their probability maps in turn. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: Numbered source subdivisions retain their original identifiers and sampled contours. Histological interpretation is recorded separately from these source region definitions.

scenes.title: Substantia nigra and numbered source subregions
scenes.prompt: Inspect the original nigral field and each numbered source subdivision at the native image resolution. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: The source describes subregion 1 as compatible with reticulata and subregion 2 as compatible with compacta. Treat these as source interpretations of the displayed regions, with histological confirmation as a separate evidence layer.

scenes.title: Midline raphe source fields
scenes.prompt: Move through adjacent sections while comparing the separately supplied midline fields. Return to the recorded point before magnifying. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: Midline labels retain the delivered source inventory and its coverage. Compare their separate regional positions and source definitions.

scenes.title: Caudal raphe source regions with olivary context
scenes.prompt: Inspect the small caudal raphe fields with paired inferior olivary source context. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: Each source field remains an independent region. The view supports spatial comparison; anatomical connectivity requires its own source evidence.

scenes.title: Linear raphe and tegmental source complexes
scenes.prompt: Compare the original complex names and locate their native probability support in complete FA sections. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: Combined source regions retain their combined definitions. Study their positions and extents; constituent identity, neurotransmitter assignment and functional connections require separate evidence.

scenes.title: Isthmic and parvicellular reticular source pairs
scenes.prompt: Follow these independently supplied source pairs through the native template and compare adjacent sections. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: The source definition of PCRtA specifies its alpha part. This view retains that exact regional scope in its native atlas space.

scenes.title: Lateral and medial geniculate source pairs
scenes.prompt: Observe the paired diencephalic fields in their explicitly supplied template grid. Compare each selected probability map with its source mask. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: These geniculate fields belong to the diencephalic part of the same source release. Compare their original extents here; cross-atlas correspondence is established separately.

scenes.title: Subthalamic fields and numbered subdivisions
scenes.prompt: Compare the source parent fields and numbered subdivisions on both sides. Use visibility controls to inspect each independently. Start with Full sections; Magnify at cursor retains the same physical source point.
scenes.note: Numbered subdivisions retain the source-specific definitions. Motor, associative and limbic interpretations require a separately supported mapping.
